recognize_zh: CD3/CD5 散佈圖中，閘門 R 內有一大群 CD5 強陽性但表面 CD3 陰性的藍色細胞，和右上方 CD3+CD5+ 的正常 T 細胞（紅色）分開；這種表面 CD3 陰性（sCD3−）的 T 細胞族群是淋巴球型 HES 的典型免疫表型。
features: Flow cytometry dot plot: CD3-PC5.5 (x-axis) versus CD5-PB (y-axis), panel C
Gated population R (blue): bright CD5 expression with absent surface CD3
Normal T cells (red) are CD3-bright and CD5-positive
Small green population with CD3 positivity and dimmer CD5
Orange CD3-negative, CD5-negative events (B/NK cells) and scattered purple events near the origin
describe_en: Flow cytometric dot plot of CD3 versus CD5 demonstrates a large, discrete population (gate R, blue) that expresses bright CD5 but lacks surface CD3, clearly separated from the normal CD3+CD5+ T cells (red) and the CD3-/CD5- non-T lymphocytes (orange). Combined with the CD4-positive, CD7-negative profile shown in the companion plots, this surface CD3-negative T-cell population is an aberrant immunophenotype. Findings are consistent with the lymphocytic variant of hypereosinophilic syndrome.

ddx.vs: CLL cells are also CD3-negative and CD5-positive but co-express CD19, CD20 (dim) and CD23 with light-chain restriction, and are CD5 dim rather than T-cell bright; B-cell markers resolve this.
Another CD5+CD3- population, but it is a B-cell neoplasm (CD19+, CD20 bright, cyclin D1+) rather than a CD4+ T-cell population.
Sezary cells are usually surface CD3-positive (sometimes dim) CD4+CD7-/CD26- with cutaneous disease, whereas complete surface CD3 loss with hypereosinophilia favors lymphocytic HES.
